pageCache.pageTitle: Sussex APC | Alternative Provision College Across Sussex
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Sussex Alternative Provision College
Sussex APC is where young people move forward with purpose, reconnecting with learning, building skills, and stepping into their next chapter.
A Quick Introduction to Sussex APC
Our college creates a structured, supportive space for students to develop self-regulation, rediscover motivation, and prepare for a successful return to mainstream school or their next stage in education. We’re here to give young people the tools, belief, and momentum to move forward and to remind them that progress is always possible.
Our ethos is simple
Reengage with learning, themselves, and their community.
Refocus on strengths, goals, and skills for life.
Reintegrate into education, training, or work and ready to succeed.
From preparing for their next setting to exploring future employment, we help students find pathways that work for them. This is where potential turns into progress.
An Introduction from our Executive Head Teacher
We offer full-time places for children and young people who have been permanently excluded, are at risk of exclusion, or are out of school for medical reasons. Our hospital school also provides specialist education for pupils who need support while unwell, while our Blended Learning Team delivers tailored packages for those requiring flexible, medical-based learning. In addition, our 3R Team supports mainstream schools by offering proactive strategies to help pupils manage challenges early and remain engaged in education.
At APC, we believe in giving every learner a fresh start, helping them rebuild confidence, reignite ambition, and prepare for the next stage of their journey. We understand that education is lifelong, and we address both the emotional and academic needs of our students to ensure lasting progress.
Whether you’re a pupil, parent, carer, or visitor, I’d like to warmly welcome you to Sussex APC. I hope your experience reflects the pride, purpose, and passion that define our community.
— Doug Thomas, Executive Head Teacher
What Makes Sussex APC Different?
We don’t define young people by what’s gone wrong. Instead, we recognise what they bring with them: resilience, creativity, determination. Our role is to build on those strengths and back students to take their next steps with confidence.
Success here looks different for everyone. It might be gaining qualifications, improving attendance, learning a life skill, or finding the courage to try something new. Whatever the milestone, our focus is on progress that lasts.
At the heart of everything is safety and support. Our safeguarding culture ensures every young person is protected, respected, and given the space to thrive.

pageCache.pageTitle: APC Curriculum Access Team | CAT Support Sussex
pageCache.text:
APC Curriculum Access Team (CAT)
Overview
Rooted in Alternative Provision, the team works alongside schools to provide the right help, at the right time, in the right place, bridging the gap between need and provision so every child can stay, belong, and succeed.
CAT offers flexible, intervention-led support that complements each school’s existing approach. Interventions are tailored to the individual pupil and adapt as their needs change, with a focus on enabling access to learning, addressing challenges early, and promoting positive behaviour for learning through targeted support, consultancy, and staff development.
Our support covers a wide range of areas to meet diverse needs, including SEND, mental health, youth crime prevention, and behaviour intervention. We also deliver programmes that build wellbeing and engagement, such as boxing for confidence, psychological support, and accessible curriculum pathways that ensure every learner can achieve success in a way that suits them. Through APC Online, students can access flexible learning opportunities, while our 3R Team (Reengage, Refocus, Reintegrate) works proactively to support reintegration and inclusion.
Support may include one-to-one mentoring, small group work, and targeted emotional and social development sessions. The team collaborates closely with school staff, families, and professionals to ensure consistent support that continues beyond their direct involvement.
CAT gives schools capacity without complexity, strengthening staff confidence, promoting inclusion, and helping students develop self-regulation, life skills, and a sense of belonging. The result is earlier intervention, reduced exclusions, and stronger, more inclusive school communities where young people are seen, supported, and given the opportunity to succeed.
Key Information
Curriculum & Opportunities

pageCache.pageTitle: APC Blended Learning & COAST | Flexible Education Support Sussex
pageCache.text:
APC Blended Learning & COAST
Overview
By combining face to face teaching with online learning, we ensure every young person remains connected to education and continues to make progress. Each student follows a bespoke programme shaped around their needs, abilities, and aspirations, delivered by specialist staff who understand the importance of trust, consistency, and encouragement.
Our provision also works alongside COAST (Crisis Outreach Acute Support Team), a Pan Sussex multidisciplinary service supporting young people as an alternative to hospital admission or as part of a supported discharge. Young people receiving Intensive Home Treatment through COAST can continue their education through a personalised package developed in partnership with families, schools, health professionals, and other services involved in their care.
Across Blended Learning and COAST, the focus is on maintaining a meaningful connection to education while supporting each young person’s health and wellbeing. We help students re-engage, refocus, and prepare for their next setting, whether that is school, further education, training, or employment, giving them the structure and support to move forward with confidence.
Key Information
Curriculum & Opportunities

At Sussex APC, assessment is about recognising progress, building confidence, and keeping every student moving forward.
We use a variety of in-class methods (from practical activities to peer review and self-evaluation), to capture learning in real time. Feedback is clear and constructive so students know exactly what they’ve done well and what to work on next.
We are an all-through school, supporting students from Reception through Key Stages 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. Our curriculum is designed to close gaps in learning and progress, offering access to 18 GCSE subjects and a range of OCN-accredited courses that provide flexible, accessible pathways for every learner. We assess Key Stage 3 and 4 pupils against aspirational GCSE grades (1–9) and provide half-termly and termly reports showing whether students are on track, working towards, or exceeding their targets. Teachers highlight mastered skills and identify next steps, ensuring every learner can see their progress clearly and continue building confidence in their achievements.
This approach makes learning personal, with the right balance of support and challenge for each student. Parents and carers are kept informed through regular communication and termly review days, where they can meet with tutors to celebrate achievements and discuss next steps.
Explore our Curriculum
Our curriculum is designed to do more than fill timetables. It helps students re-engage with learning, refocus their ambitions, and prepare for their next step through a combination of academic subjects, practical skills, personal development, and tailored support. Every subject has a clear accreditation route, with opportunities including English Language and Literature, Science and Maths, Art through AQA, Digital Media through OCN, Personal Development through WJEC, and Food Technology through BTEC.
Whether students are working towards GCSEs, recognised vocational qualifications, or developing practical skills and confidence, learning is shaped around their individual strengths, needs, and aspirations. The aim is to ensure every young person can work towards meaningful outcomes and move forward with purpose and belief in what they can achieve.
Art & Design
Art & Design at Sussex APC gives students the freedom to explore, create, and express themselves. Through projects that include drawing, painting, photography, textiles, and mixed media, students develop both technical skill and creative confidence. Lessons encourage experimentation, imagination, and problem-solving, helping young people find their own artistic voice.
Students have opportunities to showcase their work within Sussex APC and across the wider community, gaining pride and recognition for their achievements. The subject also supports a range of accredited qualifications and opens pathways into further study and careers in the creative industries.
Careers
Preparing young people for life beyond school is a key part of our Key Stage 4 curriculum. Through our Personal Development programme, pupils work towards the WJEC Preparing for Adulthood externally accredited qualification, developing the knowledge, confidence and practical skills needed to become independent, responsible and successful young adults.
This is strengthened through a comprehensive careers education programme, meaningful work experience opportunities and a wide range of enrichment activities. Together, these experiences enable pupils to develop the personal qualities and employability skills valued by employers, including communication, teamwork, resilience, problem-solving and responsibility, whilst encouraging them to make a positive contribution to their local communities and wider society.
Our ambition is that every young person leaves West Sussex Alternative Provision College with not only recognised qualifications, but also the confidence, skills and aspirations to progress successfully into further education, employment or training. We believe that success is measured not only by the qualifications our pupils achieve, but by the confident, resilient and responsible young adults they become.
Download Provider Assurance Document
English
At West Sussex Alternative Provision College, our English curriculum is designed to ensure that every pupil has the opportunity to achieve a recognised qualification that supports their future education, employment and training.
Our primary qualification offer is AQA GCSE English Language and GCSE English Literature. Pupils follow a carefully sequenced curriculum that develops reading, writing and spoken language skills whilst building the knowledge and confidence required for success at GCSE. Teaching is tailored to individual starting points, enabling pupils to make strong progress regardless of previous educational experiences.
For a small number of pupils who are not yet able to access GCSE Level 2 content, we offer Functional Skills English. This provides an alternative pathway, focusing on the practical literacy skills needed for everyday life, further learning and employment. Where appropriate, pupils are supported to progress from Functional Skills towards GCSE study as their confidence and attainment develop.
Our ambition is for every pupil to leave West Sussex Alternative Provision College with the strongest possible English qualification, ensuring they are well prepared for their next stage of education or employment.
Food Technology
Food Technology at Sussex APC combines essential life skills with practical, industry-ready knowledge. Students learn the fundamentals of cooking, nutrition, and food hygiene while gaining confidence in the kitchen. Lessons are hands-on and focus on building independence, creativity, and teamwork. Alongside developing practical skills for everyday life, learners explore pathways into the hospitality and catering industries and work towards recognised qualifications in food preparation and service.
Hospital Education
Delivered at APC Haywards Heath (The Harbour Unit)
The Harbour Unit is West Sussex Alternative Provision College's specialist hospital school, providing education for children and young people receiving inpatient mental health care. Working in partnership with clinical and therapeutic teams, we ensure that every pupil continues to access high-quality education throughout their admission, helping them maintain academic progress whilst supporting their recovery.
Our curriculum is built around the understanding that no two young people are the same. Mental health presentations, treatment plans and educational experiences vary considerably, so every programme of learning is carefully personalised to meet individual needs. By combining education with therapeutic support, we create a safe, structured environment where pupils can rebuild confidence, re-engage with learning and experience success at a pace that is right for them.
Core English and Mathematics form the foundation of our curriculum and are delivered through highly personalised one-to-one teaching. This enables learning to be tailored to each young person's current attainment, emotional readiness and future aspirations, ensuring that they continue to make meaningful academic progress during their stay. Qualifications range from Functional Skills through to GCSE, with opportunities to support learners studying Level 3 and A Level programmes where appropriate.
Alongside core subjects, pupils are encouraged to access a broad range of vocational and practical learning opportunities, including Art, Food Studies, Science, Information Technology, Horticulture and Physical Activity. These subjects provide much more than qualification opportunities; they help young people rediscover interests, develop practical life skills, improve confidence and build resilience. The curriculum has been carefully designed so that education complements each young person's therapeutic journey, supporting emotional wellbeing alongside academic achievement.
Education at The Harbour is fully integrated within the wider multidisciplinary team. Teachers work closely with clinicians, therapists and ward staff to ensure that learning reflects each young person's health, recovery goals and clinical needs. This collaborative approach allows education to remain flexible whilst providing the consistency and routine that many pupils need during periods of significant challenge.
Our ambition is that every young person leaves The Harbour with renewed confidence, recognised achievement where appropriate, and a clear pathway back into education. Whether returning to their previous school, moving into further education or progressing to another setting, we work with families and professionals to ensure each learner is well prepared for their next step.
ICT & Media Studies
ICT and Media at Sussex APC go hand in hand, giving students the tools to understand, create, and thrive in a digital world. Lessons combine practical computing and software skills with creative exploration across coding, design, and digital media. Students learn to use technology safely and responsibly while building confidence through hands-on projects in film, photography, editing, and visual storytelling. The curriculum encourages critical thinking about the media we consume and create, helping learners develop digital literacy, problem-solving skills, and an understanding of how technology shapes communication today. These skills open pathways to further study and future careers in creative, media, and digital industries.
Maths
Maths at Sussex APC is made practical, relevant, and achievable for every learner. Lessons focus on applying skills to real-life contexts like budgeting, measurement, and data handling, helping students see the value of what they learn. With step-by-step support, pupils build confidence and competence at their own pace, progressing through tailored pathways including Entry Level and GCSE qualifications. This approach ensures that every young person can develop a solid understanding of maths and use it meaningfully beyond the classroom.
OCN
We recognise that success looks different for every young person. Alongside our GCSE and Functional Skills pathways, we offer a wide range of Open College Network (OCN) qualifications, enabling pupils to achieve nationally recognised accreditation in areas that reflect their interests, strengths and future aspirations.
OCN qualifications are flexible, unit-based awards that allow pupils to develop technical knowledge and practical skills through a personalised programme of learning. This approach enables learners to build a portfolio of achievement, celebrating progress and recognising success in meaningful vocational and life skill areas.

Whilst external accreditation is primarily available to pupils in Key Stage 4, all year groups have the opportunity to participate in vocational learning and begin building their portfolios of evidence. This ensures that every young person develops practical skills, experiences success and is well prepared to progress towards accredited qualifications as they move through the school.
Our OCN offer complements the wider curriculum by developing employability skills, independence, confidence and aspiration, helping every young person leave West Sussex Alternative Provision College with recognised achievements that prepare them for further education, employment and adult life.

Construction
Hospitality & Catering

Enterprise
Creative Industries

Mechanics & Cycle Maintenance
PE (Physical Education)
PE at Sussex APC supports every student’s physical health, mental wellbeing, and sense of personal achievement. Lessons include a wide range of sports and activities designed for all abilities, encouraging participation, teamwork, and enjoyment. Students learn the value of resilience, leadership, and collaboration, developing skills that extend beyond the pitch or gym. With an emphasis on building confidence and healthy habits for life, PE helps young people discover the power of movement and the importance of staying active for their future wellbeing.
Personal Development
Personal Development, including Religious Education, equips students with the skills, values, and awareness they need to thrive in life. Lessons focus on emotional regulation, confidence, and social skills, alongside citizenship, healthy relationships, and preparation for adulthood. Students are encouraged to explore different beliefs and cultures with respect, curiosity, and critical thinking, linking their learning to real-world life skills, community understanding, and positive decision-making. Parents and carers may withdraw their child from Religious Education; please speak with your Head of School if you would like to discuss this.
Preparation for Adulthood
Preparing young people for life beyond school is a key part of our Key Stage 4 curriculum. Through our Personal Development programme, pupils work towards the WJEC Preparing for Adulthood externally accredited qualification, developing the knowledge, confidence and practical skills needed to become independent, responsible and successful young adults.
This is strengthened through a comprehensive careers education programme, meaningful work experience opportunities and a wide range of enrichment activities. Together, these experiences enable pupils to develop the personal qualities and employability skills valued by employers, including communication, teamwork, resilience, problem-solving and responsibility, whilst encouraging them to make a positive contribution to their local communities and wider society.
Our ambition is that every young person leaves West Sussex Alternative Provision College with not only recognised qualifications, but also the confidence, skills and aspirations to progress successfully into further education,

pageCache.pageTitle: APC 3R Team | Inclusion & Behaviour Support Sussex
pageCache.text:
APC 3R Team
Overview
Reengage. Refocus. Reintegrate.
Our experienced practitioners work closely with each pupil, helping them understand and manage their emotions and behaviour through targeted, relationship-based intervention. We listen carefully, take their experiences seriously, and work alongside them to build confidence, develop healthier choices, and move forward with pride.
We recognise that every young person is unique. That is why our support is highly personalised, whether it involves one-to-one mentoring, small group sessions, emotional regulation strategies, social skills development, or help with reengaging in learning. Our goal is to create meaningful, lasting change that keeps pupils connected to their school, strengthens their sense of belonging, and helps them make positive progress.
We work collaboratively with school staff, leadership teams, and families, offering practical guidance and behaviour support that strengthens inclusive practice across schools. Together, we create learning environments where young people feel safe, understood, and able to succeed.
Referrals to the APC 3R Team can be made through the Alternative Provision or Inclusion Support Referral route via the West Sussex Dashboard. Parents and carers play an essential role in this process, and we work in partnership to ensure each child receives the support they need.
Key Information
Curriculum & Opportunities

APC Brighton & Hove
Overview
Education sessions take place each day, with our team working closely with each young person’s home school or college. Learning is personalised around their existing studies, individual circumstances and treatment, helping to maintain consistency and reduce disruption to their education during the programme.
With a small number of young people attending at any one time, the provision allows education and recovery to work closely together. Our approach gives students the opportunity to continue progressing academically while rebuilding confidence, developing independence and maintaining an important connection with life beyond treatment.
Throughout their time with us, we work alongside families, education settings and health professionals to prepare for what comes next. The aim is to make the transition back into their school, college or next setting as positive and manageable as possible.
Key Information
Curriculum & Opportunities

pageCache.pageTitle: APC Burgess Hill | Sussex Alternative Provision College
pageCache.text:
APC Burgess Hill
Overview
Alongside academic progress, we place strong emphasis on life skills, behaviour for learning, and emotional development, helping students understand what’s right and wrong, build self-regulation, and make positive choices both inside and outside the classroom.
Behaviour intervention is a core part of our approach, with targeted strategies and staff who model calm, consistent, and compassionate behaviour management. Every young person is supported to develop respect, accountability, and resilience, while learning the social and emotional tools they need to succeed in wider life.
The APC Curriculum Access Team (CAT) also works closely with our centre and local schools, providing flexible, early interventions that help students remain in education and thrive in their current setting wherever possible.
At Burgess Hill, learning is personal, relationships are at the heart of progress, and every step forward, whether that be academic or emotional, is recognised and celebrated.
Key Information
Curriculum & Opportunities

pageCache.pageTitle: APC Chichester | Primary Alternative Provision Sussex
pageCache.text:
APC Chichester
Overview
Each student follows a personalised learning plan focused on building trust, curiosity, and confidence, with creativity and practical learning embedded throughout. We blend core academic subjects with hands-on projects and outdoor learning to encourage independence, teamwork, and self-belief.
Behaviour intervention plays a key role at Chichester, supporting young people to recognise their choices, understand how their actions affect themselves and others, and develop stronger emotional regulation. Through behaviour for learning and targeted support, students are encouraged to reflect, navigate challenging situations positively, and build skills that strengthen both their wellbeing and engagement with education.
Our work extends beyond the classroom. We collaborate closely with families, local services, and the APC Curriculum Access Team (CAT), which supports schools through targeted, early interventions that help prevent exclusion and promote inclusion. This partnership ensures that young people stay connected to education and receive consistent, joined-up support across all settings.
At Chichester, every young person is seen, valued, and encouraged to discover what they’re capable of not just in school, but in life.
Key Information
Curriculum & Opportunities

pageCache.pageTitle: APC Crawley | KS3 & KS4 Alternative Provision
pageCache.text:
APC Crawley
Overview
We support a diverse KS3 and KS4 community, providing education that helps students achieve qualifications, build confidence, and develop the skills needed to succeed both in school and beyond.
Behaviour intervention is a central part of what we do, helping young people build emotional regulation, develop positive behaviour for learning, and understand the impact of their choices. Through reflective work, life skills sessions, and supportive relationships, we help students make confident, informed decisions that strengthen both their learning and wellbeing.
We also work closely with the APC Curriculum Access Team (CAT), which supports schools with early, intervention-led strategies that prevent exclusion and promote inclusion. This collaboration ensures continuity for learners, keeping them connected to their education and supported at every stage.
At Crawley, we combine clear goals with genuine care and support. Careers guidance, vocational pathways, and tailored academic programmes sit alongside social and emotional development. Our partnerships with community groups, and schools open doors for young people to re-engage, refocus, and reintegrate into education or employment, with the confidence to move forward and the belief that they can.
Key Information
Curriculum & Opportunities

APC Haywards Heath
Overview
Our team provides education from Key Stage 3 through to Key Stage 5, with personalised timetables shaped around each student’s individual needs, circumstances and goals. A broad range of academic and creative subjects is complemented by enrichment opportunities, helping young people continue making progress while supporting their social, emotional and physical wellbeing.
Working closely with health professionals, families and each young person’s school or college, we help maintain continuity during their time at Haywards Heath. Education is about more than keeping up with learning. It provides routine, purpose and opportunities to rebuild confidence at a time when other areas of life may feel uncertain.
Preparing for what comes next is an important part of the provision. Learning and transition planning work together to help young people maintain progress and feel ready to move into their next setting with greater confidence.
Key Information
Curriculum & Opportunities

pageCache.pageTitle: APC Lancing | Alternative Provision for Young People
pageCache.text:
APC Lancing
Overview
Here, structured teaching is balanced with creativity and curiosity, helping young people grow academically, socially, and emotionally. Every lesson is designed to engage learners, build confidence, and foster the independence they need to move forward with purpose.
Behaviour intervention plays a key role in our approach, helping young people build emotional awareness, develop positive behaviour for learning, and strengthen essential life skills. Through reflective practice, open discussion, and targeted support, students learn to manage challenges, make positive choices, and better understand the impact of their actions within a safe and supportive environment.
We also collaborate with the APC Curriculum Access Team (CAT), which supports schools through proactive, intervention-led work aimed at preventing exclusion. CAT provides guidance and strategies that promote positive behaviour, enabling students to stay engaged in learning and remain part of their school communities.
At Lancing, pastoral care underpins everything we do. Families are actively involved in their child’s journey, and strong community connections ensure each learner is supported both inside and outside the classroom. Our aim is simple: to help every young person re-engage, refocus, and reintegrate not just into education, but into life with confidence and self-belief.
Key Information
Curriculum & Opportunities

APC Littlehampton
Overview
Housed within a beautiful Grade II listed building, it provides a sense of stability and belonging; a place where young people are supported to grow both academically and personally.
The team here takes a balanced approach, combining clear structure with creativity, and care with challenge. Behaviour intervention is an important part of this, helping young people build self-awareness, strengthen emotional regulation, and develop vital life skills. Through consistent support and positive relationships, students learn to navigate challenges, make constructive choices, and apply these skills both in and beyond the classroom.
We also work closely with the APC Curriculum Access Team (CAT), which supports schools through early, flexible interventions that reduce the need for exclusion. This partnership ensures continuity for learners and helps create a strong behaviour-for-learning culture across both our centre and local schools.
At Littlehampton, learning goes far beyond the classroom. Alongside core academic subjects and vocational pathways, students take part in enrichment activities that build teamwork, resilience, and leadership. Every programme is designed to help young people discover their strengths, gain qualifications, and prepare for their next step, whether that’s reintegration into school, further education, or training. This is a centre that doesn’t just teach lessons; it helps shape futures.
Key Information
Curriculum & Opportunities

pageCache.pageTitle: APC Worthing | Anxiety Learning Centre & AP Provision
pageCache.text:
APC Worthing
Overview
Placements are agreed through the CAT referral process and typically last between 6 and 12 weeks, with clear outcomes identified from the start. The focus is on helping young people rebuild confidence, reconnect with learning, and prepare for a successful transition back to their school.
Pupils learn in a calm, nurturing environment alongside others who may be experiencing similar challenges. Alongside a broad curriculum, personalised pastoral support and targeted interventions help pupils develop emotional resilience, independence, and practical strategies to support their return to school.
Every placement has a clear exit route. The Worthing Anxiety Centre is a focused intervention rather than a long term placement, giving young people the skills, confidence, and support they need to move successfully back into their next setting.

Colm Gallagher
Colm is an accomplished educational leader with more than twenty‑three years’ experience driving improvement across mainstream, adult learning, and secure environments.
Holding the NPQH, he brings a strong foundation in system leadership, curriculum design, and organisational development, strengthened by roles as a primary Headteacher, an all-through Assistant Headteacher as well as a Senior Trainer and International Coach for a national coaching programme in Brunei. This international work deepened his expertise in developing staff, building coaching cultures, and delivering large‑scale professional learning.
As Deputy Head of Education at Feltham YOI, Colm led strategic development in a complex secure setting, shaping curriculum intent, strengthening teaching practice, and embedding evidence‑based approaches that raise expectations and accelerate progress. His leadership centres on clarity, relational culture, and consistent implementation, ensuring staff are empowered, learners experience ambitious teaching and provision remains stable and purposeful.
Colm has supported schools nationally and internationally to refine behaviour systems, enhance instructional practice, and embed trauma‑informed approaches.
Outside of work, he enjoys spending time with his family, walking, reading, and listening to music.
As Director of Learning, he brings strategic vision, curriculum leadership, and a relentless focus on improving the quality of education at scale.

Sam Channon
Sam joined Sussex APC in 2016 and brings over a decade of senior-level experience from both private and public sectors. Her career began in media and TV, where she gained a strong foundation in recruitment, policy development and budget management. Having completed her CIPD qualification, Sam then moved into the education sector, having discovered a real passion for making a positive difference to the lives of young people.
Since then, Sam has built extensive experience in school operations and leadership. She firmly believes that when supporting young people with the tools, belief, and momentum to move forward, lasting progress is always possible. Sam is fully committed to ensuring learners are given a fresh start - helping them rebuild confidence, reignite ambition, and prepare for a successful return to mainstream school or their next stage in education.
Sam is Level 7 CIPFA qualified, and an experienced change management expert. She drives meaningful transformation, whilst delivering results with clarity and professionalism, in collaboration with key stakeholders.
Outside of work, Sam enjoys spending time with her family, travelling, and listening to music.
Doug Thomas
Doug brings decades of experience across Alternative Provision, special educational needs, and mainstream secondary education, giving him a deep understanding of what young people need to thrive. He is driven by a simple belief: education should open doors. Under his leadership, Sussex APC focuses on creating opportunities (academic, personal, and aspirational), so that every young person can discover what they’re capable of and build habits of learning that last a lifetime.
Doug is passionate about the role of Alternative Provision as a springboard for the future. He’s incredibly proud of the many APC students who have gone on to succeed in fields such as business, the emergency services, politics, and healthcare, and he remains committed to helping the next generation follow their own paths with confidence.
Having lived and worked in Sussex since 1998, Doug has dedicated more than 2 decades of experience to education in the county. He holds a BA from the University of Kent, an MA and PGCE from Durham University, and has completed extensive specialist training in SEND and behaviour for learning. Outside of school, he’s also a qualified ECB Level 2 cricket coach, a role that reflects his belief in teamwork, resilience, and encouragement, both on and off the field.
Meet our Leadership & Management Committee
At Sussex APC, our leadership team is about presence, action, and unwavering belief in what young people can achieve. Our senior leaders and governors work together to make sure every decision supports our vision: Reengage, Refocus, Reintegrate.
We are hands-on. Our leadership team spends time in our centres talking to students, supporting staff, and making sure our ethos is lived every day. Our governors bring expertise from education, safeguarding, finance, health, and the wider community, holding us to the highest standards and ensuring we stay focused on outcomes that matter.

About Sussex APC
Sussex Alternative Provision College (APC) exists to help young people Reengage, Refocus, and Reintegrate, giving them the belief, tools, and structure they need to move forward with purpose. We’re not just here to fill time. We’re here to create momentum.
Formed in 2013 and led by Doug Thomas (Executive Head Teacher) and Sam Channon (Chief Operations Officer and Lead for Medical Education), we work closely with our Management Committee, a network of schools, and multi-agency partners to ensure every young person has a path forward.
Explore our Centres
We operate across eight centres in Burgess Hill, Crawley, Chichester, Littlehampton, Lancing, and Worthing, as well as our specialist sites in Brighton & Hove and Haywards Heath, providing 292 full-time places for primary and secondary students across Sussex. These places support young people who have been permanently excluded, are at risk of exclusion, or are unable to attend mainstream school for medical reasons.
APC 3R Team
Sussex APC is proud to offer the APC 3R Team, a specialist service that supports children and young people in schools who are finding school life difficult and may be at risk of exclusion.
APC Blended Learning & COAST
Our Blended Learning provision is the commissioned provider for West Sussex under Section 19 policy, offering a flexible and personalised approach for pupils who are unable to attend a traditional school setting due to medical or exceptional circumstances.
APC Brighton & Hove
APC Brighton & Hove supports young people receiving intensive day treatment at Spring Tide for an eating disorder, helping them maintain their learning alongside their wider treatment programme. This joined up approach keeps young people connected to education while receiving the health and wellbeing support they need within the community.
APC Burgess Hill
Our Burgess Hill Centre is a vibrant, inclusive environment serving pupils from Reception and KS1 through to KS4. It provides structure, support, and space for young people to reengage with education, refocus on their ambitions, and reintegrate into the next phase of learning or life with confidence.
APC Chichester
Our Chichester Centre is a small, nurturing environment for Reception, KS1, and KS2 pupils, where individual progress is celebrated and personal growth is central.
APC Crawley
Our Crawley Centre, set within an historic building that has been a place of learning since 1852, is a space where tradition meets innovation.
APC Curriculum Access Team (CAT)
The APC Curriculum Access Team (CAT) supports children and young people in schools who are finding school life difficult and may be at risk of exclusion. The goal is to help students Reengage with learning, Refocus on their strengths, and Reintegrate into school life with confidence.
APC Haywards Heath
APC Haywards Heath provides specialist education for young people aged 12 to 18 receiving inpatient support at The Harbour Unit for acute mental health needs, including emotional difficulties, mental health challenges and eating disorders. Based within the grounds of the Princess Royal Hospital, education forms an important part of each young person’s wider treatment and recovery.
APC Lancing
Our Lancing Centre provides a vibrant and nurturing environment for pupils from Reception through to KS4.
APC Littlehampton
Our Littlehampton Centre sits at the heart of the community, offering a creative, purposeful space where KS3 and KS4 students can reconnect with learning and rebuild their confidence.
APC Worthing
Our Worthing Centre is a modern, purpose-built environment designed to help KS3 and KS4 students feel supported, capable, and ready to achieve.
Our provision spans multiple pathways
These hours reflect the structured learning time tailored to each student’s age, needs and setting, ensuring consistent education, wellbeing support, and meaningful progress.
SMP Blended Learning Primary
SMP Blended Learning Secondary
Haywards Heath (The Harbour Unit)
Support Focused
The Brighton & Hove and Haywards Heath Centres provide an additional 31 full-time places, forming a vital part of the APC offer. They provide specialist education and wraparound support for young people with complex health and emotional needs across Sussex.
Specialist Centres
Haywards Heath also works with our COAST (Crisis Outreach Acute Support Team) to offer education as part of intensive home treatment and supported discharge, helping young people reintegrate into their community with confidence and stability.
3R Team
By working directly with schools, staff, and families, the team helps learners build self-regulation, manage behaviour, and stay engaged in education. Together, these teams form a seamless network of support, connecting health and education, sharing expertise, and helping young people take positive, lasting steps toward their future.
A Launchpad for Progress
All our centres deliver educational programmes tailored to each student’s needs, and our specialist teams go further:
Blended Learning Team
The Blended Learning Team supports young people at home due to medical reasons, creating personalised packages that keep learning moving.
Curriculum Access Team
The APC Curriculum Access Team works directly with mainstream schools, offering strategies and interventions to reduce exclusions and keep students connected to their education.
Our Ethos
We know education is a lifelong process and sometimes past events or challenges have blocked progress. That’s why we focus on building confidence, skills, and momentum so students leave here not only ready for the next step but believing they can take it.
Our Approach
Whether a student’s goal is to return to mainstream school, move on to a specialist provision, progress into further education, enter training, or secure employment, Sussex APC provides the structure, encouragement, and belief to make it happen. Our model works as a revolving door, not a final destination, supporting young people to re-engage with learning, build the skills they need, and move forward with confidence toward their next step.
I would like to welcome you all to our school and to say that whether you are a pupil, a parent/carer or someone who would like to visit us, you are most welcome and I do hope that your experience reflects the pride we feel in working at Sussex APC.
— Doug Thomas, Executive Head Teacher

Our Vision & Values
At Sussex APC, our vision and values aren’t just words on a page, they’re the way we show up for young people every single day.
We exist to Reengage, Refocus, and Reintegrate students, giving them the confidence, skills, and opportunities to move forward on their own terms. We believe every young person has something powerful to offer, and it’s our job to help them see it, strengthen it, and put it into action. Our commitment is simple: to create an environment where potential is recognised, ambition is encouraged, and futures are built, one step, one goal, one breakthrough at a time.
Our Vision
We see a future where Alternative Provision is not an afterthought, but a respected, well-resourced pillar of the education system, a place where young people are not written off but recognised for what they can achieve.
Our vision is rooted in three guiding principles:
Reengage
Building trust, curiosity, and a love of learning.
Refocus
Setting goals, identifying strengths, and working towards meaningful outcomes.
Reintegrate
Supporting young people to return to education, employment, or training with confidence and skills that last. We aim to be a national example of how AP can deliver excellence consistently, creatively, and unapologetically in the interests of young people.
Our Values
Going Against the Grain
We reject the idea that any child is beyond support or opportunity.
Commitment
We stay the course, even when the path isn’t straightforward.
Respect
Every student is treated as capable, unique, and full of potential.
Purpose
Every decision is driven by what helps young people move forward.
Care
Not just in words, but in consistent actions that build trust and belief.
